question: How many casual leave days do I get per year?
answer: Full-time employees accrue 12 casual leave days per calendar year [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements].

question: Can I carry forward unused casual leave?
answer: Yes, up to 6 days. Any unused balance above 6 days lapses permanently at the end of the calendar year, and no encashment is permitted [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward].

question: How many remote days can a Band 3 employee take?
answer: Band 3 employees may work remotely up to 2 days per calendar week, while Band 1 and 2 employees may take 3 days [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Remote Work Allowance]. Note that v1 of the same policy states 2 days for all bands, so the documents conflict on this point.

question: What happens to my unused leave if I resign, and what if I transfer to another entity mid-year?
answer: If you resign, unused casual leave lapses on your last working day and is not encashed [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward]. The documents do not say what happens to your carry-forward balance if you transfer to another entity mid-year.

question: What notice do I need to change my remote arrangement, and does that affect my leave balance?
answer: You must give at least 15 days written notice to your manager before changing an approved remote work arrangement [remote_work_policy_v1 § 3. Notice Period]. The documents do not address any interaction between a remote-arrangement change and leave balances.

question: Is there a sabbatical policy, and does it affect my casual leave accrual?
answer: The documents do not mention a sabbatical policy. They do state that casual leave accrues at 1 day per month for full-time employees [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements], so accrual during an unpaid sabbatical is not addressed either.
